## 4\. The exact additional estimate still required

For any fixed proposed controller, let \(T_{\max}\) be the maximal strong lifespan.

A sufficient continuation mechanism would be an estimate, for some \(\alpha>0\),

\[
\boxed{
\sup_{\tau\leq t<T_{\max}}
\|c\|_{C^{\alpha,\alpha/2}
(\mathbb T^3\times[\tau,t])}
\leq
Q(\tau,N,f,K,m,\chi,b)
<\infty
}
\tag{7}
\]

for each \(\tau>0\), with a bound independent of \(T_{\max}\)\.

Given (7), the matrix \(D(c)\) is Hölder continuous in space-time. Parabolic system estimates and maximal regularity can then upgrade the solution to the regularity needed for terminal continuation. This is the general architecture used in the structured-friction results.

The existing entropy estimate gives something different\:

\[
\int_0^{T_{\max}}
\sum_i\|\nabla c_i(t)\|_2^2\,dt
\leq f_+H(c_0|\bar c)
\leq f_+\log(1/m).
\tag{8}
\]

It controls an integrated \(L^2\) gradient, not the Hölder modulus in (7).

### Why even very small entropy does not close this implication

Take \(N=2\), means \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), and a smooth compactly supported function \(\phi\) in a small ball. For small \(\rho>0\), define

\[
r_\rho(x)
=a\left[
\phi\left(\frac{x-x_0}{\rho}\right)
-\rho^3\int_{\mathbb R^3}\phi
\right],
\]

with a fixed sufficiently small \(a>0\), and set

\[
c_1=\frac12+r_\rho,\qquad
c_2=\frac12-r_\rho.
\]

These compositions remain strictly within the simplex, with a uniform positive pointwise floor. Their means are exactly \(1/2\)\.

Nevertheless,

\[
H(c|\bar c)=O(\rho^3),
\qquad
\sum_i\|\nabla c_i\|_2^2=O(\rho),
\]

while

\[
\|\nabla c\|_\infty
\asymp\rho^{-1}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

Thus there is no inequality controlling the spatial Lipschitz norm from entropy and instantaneous \(L^2\) gradient energy alone, even strictly inside the simplex.

This example is not a singular Maxwell–Stefan solution and is not a counterexample to the requested controller theorem. It identifies the missing mathematical implication: **rapid entropy homogenization can coexist, at the level of admissible states, with arbitrarily concentrated spatial gradients.**

A genuine nonlinear smoothing or global regularity estimate must rule out the relevant concentration patterns along actual solutions.
